findings: No corrected-area benefit: all six cases tie. The summed-case wall increase is concentrated in complete wb_dma (+12.22s), partly offset by b20_opt (-5.67s) and i2c (-0.95s).

wb_dma scans the same 1671 initial roots but initial signature hits rise 656830→986419, positive sampled candidates 223525→304698, discovery candidates 3852→3942, proof chunks 93→99, refinement rounds 82→88, and executed refinement roots 1894→2050; final qualified candidates remain 426. This is observed work expansion under different learned constraints.

wb_dma initial-search wall rises 12.08→17.80s, proof wall 16.34→21.14s, refinement-search wall 4.61→5.97s, checkpoint wall 1.74→2.32s; guidance nonsearch residual is nearly flat 24.80→25.05s. Proof overhead cannot be separated into capture/hash/parse/load/I/O from existing timers.

b20_opt inline finishes all 4895 roots; helper has 4704 roots at its 120s limit. Guidance nonsearch residual falls 35.67→28.66s, while proof wall rises 37.41→38.84s. The helper snapshot is incomplete, so these are observed-path figures, not equal-work timings.

mem_ctrl is budget limited in both arms: last completed snapshots cover 928 helper versus 896 inline initial roots, with 413 versus 454 accepted image rows. This offsets the simple completion-count advantage: one extra complete case does not imply uniformly greater search coverage.

Large artifact hashing/parsing is repeated per model-bearing batch across three validation layers, not per candidate/model. In wb_dma the collector checks 88 distinct consumed batch bindings and rebuilds 88 proof graphs; it hashes 29.73MB of corresponding CNFs in that collector layer. Full compiled-graph evaluation still runs once per replayed model (30.15M→32.55M graph-node iterations), followed by two original-AIG steps.

No isolated timers exist for hashing, JSON/CSV parsing, model writing, CNF reconstruction, graph evaluation, original-AIG replay, or I/O waits. Attribution among these is unmeasured; no new benchmark was run.

Summed per-case transform wall is 339.78→345.53s. Serial two-worker wave wall including per-wave checks/DSEC is 276.60→269.24s because the wave critical path differs. Neither supports a pure equal-work solver-speed claim.

wb_dma ordinary SAT solve time rises only 3.935→4.259s (+0.324s) within its +4.799s proof-phase increase. Secondary SAT time removed is 1.748s. Other proof-phase work remains unseparated by the saved timers.

source_inspection.batching: InlineFrozenQueries._batch validates one model batch; solve() caches validations by manifest; collect_inline_models() caches batches by chunk+manifest and reconstructed graphs by chunk within each collection call
source_inspection.cache_hits: A later solve() call with a model-bearing cached SAT receipt revalidates its immutable files; this is per distinct batch per solve call, not per receipt
source_inspection.hypothesis_only: Repeated per-batch validation and larger per-model compiled-graph evaluation are plausible overheads; saved logs cannot isolate their time. Different learned constraints and refinement searches also change work.
source_inspection.per_model_work: bound_model is row/assumption lookup, not file I/O. d.replay_model evaluates the entire compiled graph once and original AIG twice for every model in both arms. Inline compiled graph contains all original chunk free/reset/step miters, whereas helper CNF contains only the failed image candidates
source_inspection.repeated_per_batch_work: A consumed inline batch is fully revalidated in _batch, in solve(), and again in collect_inline_models(): manifest/artifact hashing plus query/result/model parsing at each stage; collector independently rebuilds proof CNF hash once per source chunk
unmeasured: No separate timers for CNF/sidecar hashing, JSON/CSV parsing, CNF reconstruction, compiled-graph evaluation, original-AIG replay, model emission, or storage wait
solver_process_wall_s includes subprocess startup/CNF load and parent-side checks, so it is not pure SAT time

helper model_report.wall_s begins after helper CNF/query/provenance preparation; inline model_report.wall_s begins before reading/rebuilding original artifacts, so those model-report timers are not directly matched
